# Abyākata Saṁyutta (SN 44)
**ID:** SN 44
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Abyākata Saṁyutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn44
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
These tenets—including whether the world is eternal or finite, whether the soul is identical to or distinct from the body, and whether the Tathāgata exists after death—were set aside as speculative views rooted in the implicit presumption of a self and dismissed as detrimental to liberation [Bodhi 2003; Shulman 2014; SuttaCentral]. In seven of the eleven discourses, only the four permutations regarding the post-mortem status of the Tathāgata are raised, where the Tathāgata is declared beyond description, deep and unfathomable like the ocean; only two discourses, the *Moggallānasutta* (SN 44.7, PTS SN iv 391–395) and the *Vacchagottasutta* (SN 44.8, PTS SN iv 395–397), explicitly list all ten standard undeclared views, explaining their rejection through non-identification with the aggregates [Bodhi 2003; Shulman 2014]. Notable interlocutors include King Pasenadi of Kosala and the wise bhikkhunī Khemā (SN 44.1), Anurādha (SN 44.2), Moggallāna (SN 44.7), Sabhiya Kaccāna (SN 44.11), and the wanderer Vacchagotta (SN 44.8, SN 44.9, SN 44.10) [Bodhi 2003; Nyanaponika, Hecker, and Bodhi 2003; Radich 2007; Ngoc Cuong Le 2018]. In the *Ānandasutta* (SN 44.10), the Buddha maintains complete silence (*tuṇhī ahosi*) when questioned by Vacchagotta on the existence of the self, later explaining to Ānanda that affirming a self falls into eternalism, while denying it fosters annihilationism [Tao Jiang 2006; Ngoc Cuong Le 2018].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect individual suttas of SN 44 to discourses in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* collections (T 99 and T 100), including parallels for SN 44.2 (SĀ 106), SN 44.7 (SĀ 958, SĀ² 191), SN 44.8 (SĀ² 192), SN 44.10 (SĀ 961, SĀ² 195), and SN 44.11 (SĀ² 193) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus algorithmic text alignments corroborate close textual correspondence with these *Saṁyuktāgama* sections and identify matches in Sanskrit and Tibetan texts, including the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the *Dharmaskandha*, the *Avadānaśataka*, and Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse between SN 44 and related discussions on the aggregates, views, and unanswered questions, notably the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Vacchagotta Saṁyutta* (SN 33), the *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), the *Cūḷamālukya Sutta* (MN 63), and the *Aggivaccha Sutta* (MN 72) [DharmaNexus].
